name: youtube-search-api
h1: YouTube Search Results by Keyword — Ranked Videos With Full Stats
metaTitle: YouTube Search Results Scraper by Keyword | ActorForge
metaDescription: Get YouTube search results for any keyword with rank, views, likes and duration, plus date, region and length filters. Official API, from $0.30 per 1,000.
tagline: Type a keyword and get YouTube's own ranked results, each enriched with views, likes, comments, duration and tags, through the official API.
intro: Seeing what ranks on YouTube for a keyword usually means searching by hand and copying titles, with no view counts or durations in view. This actor runs **YouTube search by keyword** through the official **YouTube Data API v3** using your own free key, and returns one row per result in YouTube's search order, with `searchRank` recorded for each.

Search results on their own only carry basic snippet data, so every result is enriched with a `videos.list` lookup: title, description, channel, published date, duration in seconds, views, likes, comment count, tags, category, default language, thumbnails, live status, made-for-kids flag and a Shorts flag. You can apply YouTube's own filters: `order` (relevance, date, view count, rating or title), `publishedAfter` and `publishedBefore`, `regionCode`, `relevanceLanguage` and `videoDuration`. Setting `searchType` to channel returns channel rows instead.

It is aimed at YouTube keyword research, trend and competitor tracking, influencer discovery and content gap analysis. Results cost $0.30 per 1,000 plus $0.002 per page of 50, roughly $0.34 per 1,000 all in.
howItWorks: Each query in `searchQueries` is sent to `search.list` with your filters, 50 results per page, up to `maxResultsPerQuery`.
The video IDs on each page are looked up with `videos.list` so every row carries full stats, duration and tags.
Rows keep the query and the result's rank, and duplicates across queries are removed.
The run log shows a quota estimate before any call; each page costs 100 search units plus 1 for the video details.
Search pages that return no rows are not charged, and a `quotaExceeded` error stops the run cleanly with the rows already delivered.

useCases.title: YouTube keyword research
useCases.text: Run a list of candidate keywords and compare what ranks: view counts, durations and publish dates of the top results show how competitive each term is and what format wins.

useCases.title: Content gap analysis
useCases.text: Filter by `publishedAfter` and `order` set to date to see what has been published recently on a topic, or by view count to see what has performed best, and spot angles nobody covers well.

useCases.title: Influencer and channel discovery
useCases.text: Search a niche and look at which channels appear repeatedly in the results, or set `searchType` to channel to get channel rows with subscriber, video and view counts directly.

useCases.title: Regional and language checks
useCases.text: Use `regionCode` and `relevanceLanguage` to see results available in a given country or most relevant to a language, for example before launching content in a new market.

comparisonNote: Search is the most quota-hungry API call, so a free key tops out at about 5,000 results a day; if you need far more volume and do not mind page scraping, a no-key scraper has no quota ceiling. Results also differ slightly from what a logged-in user sees, because the API has no personalisation and no ads.

faq.q: How many YouTube search results can I get per keyword?
faq.a: YouTube caps search depth at about 500 results per query, so `maxResultsPerQuery` goes up to 500. For more coverage, split a topic into narrower queries or separate date ranges with `publishedAfter` and `publishedBefore`.

faq.q: Why does YouTube search use so much API quota?
faq.a: YouTube charges 100 quota units for each `search.list` page of up to 50 results, plus 1 unit here for the video details. With 10,000 free units a day, one key gives about 100 pages, or roughly 5,000 results.

faq.q: Will the results match what I see on youtube.com?
faq.a: They are YouTube's own search ranking for an API request, with no personalisation and no ads. They can differ slightly from what a logged-in user sees in the browser.

faq.q: How do I search for YouTube Shorts only?
faq.a: The API does not flag Shorts. Set `videoDuration` to short to get videos under 4 minutes, and use the `isShort` heuristic in each row (3 minutes or less and not live) to narrow further.

faq.q: What does a search run cost?
faq.a: Results cost $0.0003 each and each page of up to 50 results that returned rows costs $0.002. So 50 results cost $0.017, and 1,000 results cost about $0.34.
